description: Write pages and change them. A body is clean semantic HTML (h2 and h3 sections, paragraphs, links), no styles or scripts. Every page gets a title card as its featured image. A picture in the body is a screenshot of a real page (update_page_images screenshot: a product you name, its pricing) or your own upload, then its returned URL goes in an . action: - create(title, primaryKeyword, contentHtml?, metaTitle?, metaDescription?, excerpt?, slug?, question?, articleType?, pageType?, subject?, destination?, schedule?): A new page, with your body or empty. The duplicate check runs first and duplicateCheck names a page this one may repeat (improve that one instead), but never stops it. pageType makes a comparison, alternatives, integration or use_case page about subject, in its type's destination (refused while that destination is switched off). destination puts a blog-style page in one of the owner's own folders. It is yours to write (sightkickWrites off; update_page edit sightkickWrites: true hands it to Sightkick). Without schedule it waits in Unscheduled: ready with a body, planned without. schedule: next (the next open slot) or a day puts it on the schedule, where it goes live that day exactly as written. publish_page publish sends it now. next says how it goes out. - edit(articleId, contentHtml?, edits?, primaryKeyword?, title?, metaTitle?, metaDescription?, excerpt?, slug?, articleType?, question?, questions?, notes?, baseHash?, reason?, minor?, sightkickWrites?, destination?): Change a page: contentHtml replaces the whole body, or edits change parts of it, each find an exact passage of the body as get_pages page includeContent returns it, appearing once (none is made if one misses). A live page, at any age, needs baseHash (get_pages page) and goes to the site with publish_page republish. Say why in reason: it stays on the page's record, where the change is measured from the day it goes out. Its Updated date moves only when its words change: links, formatting and pictures keep it, and so does a correction marked minor. primaryKeyword re-aims the page at another keyword at any stage, live too, keeping its id and record; change the title and body to match in the same edit. The slug and destination only before it's live, the type and brief only before it's written. - delete(articleId): Delete a page that never went live. Can't be undone. - register(url, query, prompt?, title?, articleType?, liveSince?): Record a page you shipped yourself (a repo, the CMS), so it's tracked like Sightkick's: index, Search Console, AI citations. query is its main search, prompt the buyer's question it answers. Again on the same URL updates it. - unregister(pageId): Stop tracking a registered page (get_pages shipped). The site doesn't change. - log_change(url, what, commit?): Record a change you made to a live page yourself, so its result is read over the next weeks (get_activity receipt with the changeId). An update_page edit needs none: it is measured once it goes out.
name: update_page
title: Write and change pages
